plain.li: [spring] Planting from first light to last. My back gave out before the light did.
[spring] Longer days, and the work stretches to fill every hour of them.
[spring] Mud on everything and tired to the bone. Spring is hard on the legs.
[summer] Up at dawn to beat the heat, and still working when it came. Asleep on my feet by supper.
[summer] Kept working because it was still light, and it stayed light far too long.
[summer] Too hot to sleep last night, and too much to do today to make up for it.
[fall] Harvest. I carried more baskets today than I could count, and I tried.
[fall] Brought in the last of the field before the frost. I could sleep for a week.
[fall] Racing the frost on no sleep and cold porridge.
[winter] Hauled firewood until dark. My arms are still shaking.
[winter] The cold wears you out even sitting still.
[winter] Dark at both ends of the day, and I worked through both.
[lowmood] Tired, and it isn't the kind of tired that sleep fixes.
[trait:Nervous] Lay awake worrying, then worked all day on no sleep. Tomorrow will be worse.

warm.li: Tired out. Still, I got done what I said I would.

blunt.li: Slept four hours. Worked twelve. Bad sums.

cheerful.li: Tired enough to sleep standing up, and proud of every bit of today.

gloomy.li: Tired again. It's the one thing I can count on.

cold.li: Fatigue is a resource like any other, and we're spending ours too fast.

plain.li: [spring] Damp spring air, and it aches every time the weather turns.
[spring] Watched the others plant from the doorway. Walking that far still hurts.
[spring] The rain set it throbbing all night.
[summer] Sweat gets under the dressing and stings. I changed it twice today.
[summer] Too hot to lie still and too sore to move. I did a bit of both.
[summer] Sat in the shade all day nursing it. The others brought me water.
[fall] Harvest time, and I can barely carry a bowl. I counted the baskets instead.
[fall] The cold mornings set it aching before I'm out of bed.
[fall] Tried to help in the fields and had to stop before noon.
[winter] The cold gets in where it hurts and settles there.
[winter] Lay close to the fire all evening, turning the bad side toward it.
[winter] Every step on the frozen ground jars it.
[hurt] The doctor says it's healing. It doesn't feel like it.
[old] Pain takes longer to leave at my age. This one has settled in for the season.

warm.li: The others keep finding reasons to sit with me. I know what they're doing, and I'm grateful.

blunt.li: Still hurts. Still working.

cheerful.li: Took ten steps without wincing today. Celebrating with a lie-down.

gloomy.li: I measure the days by how much they hurt. Today was a bad one.

cold.li: Pain is information. Today it said rest, so I rested.

plain.li: [spring] The barracks windows are open again. Fresh air, and a dozen snores to go with it.
[spring] Mud on every boot in the barracks. Someone needs to sweep, and it won't be me.
[spring] Woke to birdsong and somebody's elbow.
[summer] The barracks are stifling. All of us breathing the same hot air all night.
[summer] Someone left the barracks door open for the breeze and let the insects in.
[summer] Slept on top of the blanket in the barracks, and so did the rest of them.
[fall] The barracks smell of wet coats now. They'll smell of wet coats until spring.
[fall] One cough has gone round the whole barracks.
[fall] Fought over the bed by the warm wall again. Lost.
[winter] Packed into the barracks for the warmth. I can feel someone breathing on my neck.
[winter] Someone's cold feet found their way into my bed in the night.
[winter] The barracks are the warmest room in the colony, and the least private.
[lowmood] In the barracks I can't even be miserable in private.

warm.li: Lent my spare blanket to the bed next to mine. The barracks are like that.

blunt.li: Barracks. Again. Still no door.

cheerful.li: Another night of the barracks choir. I'm sure two of them snore in tune.

gloomy.li: Lay awake in the barracks listening to everyone else sleep.

cold.li: I know everyone's habits now: who snores, who talks, who takes blankets. Useful, if not restful.

plain.li: [spring] Bright day outside and a dark workshop inside. I kept stepping out to rest my eyes.
[spring] Worked in the dim storeroom while the sun was out. Like being shut in a box.
[spring] The rainy days are dark enough without a dark room on top of them.
[summer] Even on a summer day the back rooms are like a cave.
[summer] Came in from the bright fields and couldn't see a thing for a minute.
[summer] Long days outside, and the storeroom is still black as night.
[fall] The days are getting shorter, and the rooms aren't getting any lighter.
[fall] Dark by supper now, and the hall darker still.
[fall] Spent the afternoon sorting the harvest by feel.
[winter] We go easy on the light in winter. My eyes ache by evening.
[winter] Dark all day in the workshop and dark all night outside it.
[winter] Shutters closed against the cold. It's been dusk indoors since morning.
[lowtech] One torch for the whole storeroom. I worked in the half of the room it reached.
[!lowtech] The light in the corridor flickers. I counted the flickers instead of working.

warm.li: Lit the lamp in the back room before the others came in, so nobody would trip.

blunt.li: Dark again. I want a window.

cheerful.li: Worked in the dark so long I'm sure I can see like a cat now.

gloomy.li: It was dark when I came in this morning, and it stayed dark.

cold.li: Every room without light costs us an hour a day. I've done the sum.

plain.li: [spring] Wore through both knees of my pants planting.
[spring] Spring rain and a coat full of holes. I'm wetter inside it than out.
[spring] Thorns took a strip out of my sleeve clearing the brush.
[summer] Too hot for a coat anyway, which is just as well, since mine is in pieces.
[summer] My hat has a hole in the brim exactly where the sun comes through.
[summer] Sweat has rotted the collar off my shirt.
[fall] Patched my coat with an old sack before the cold comes. It'll do. It'll have to.
[fall] The wind's picking up and my clothes are giving up.
[fall] Snagged my shirt on the fence and lost half the back of it.
[winter] My coat is more holes than coat, and it's winter.
[winter] Stuffed straw into my boots to fill the holes. It helps, some.
[winter] I'm wearing two worn shirts to make one whole one.
[poor] We're all in rags here. Mine are just worse.

warm.li: Gave my last good shirt to the newcomer. I've got patches; they had nothing.

blunt.li: Holes everywhere. Need cloth.

cheerful.li: Lost a sleeve today. Now I've got one cool arm and one warm one.

gloomy.li: My clothes look the way I feel.

cold.li: Traders will judge the colony by these rags. So will raiders.

plain.li: [spring] Ate on the doorstep in the spring sun. Better than the floor, at least.
[spring] Muddy floor, no table, bowl on my knees.
[spring] We ate sitting on the woodpile. It has nails in it.
[summer] Ate outside on the grass, because there's nowhere better inside.
[summer] Ate standing up in the shade. The ants found my bowl before I did.
[summer] Supper on a stump in the yard. Too hot to mind much.
[fall] Ate sitting on a sack of the harvest. Soft, and it smelled of grain.
[fall] The wind blew leaves into my bowl while I ate on the step.
[fall] We sat on the floor around the harvest baskets and ate from our laps.
[winter] Ate crouched by the fire with the bowl on my knees. My legs went numb.
[winter] Too cold for the step, so we ate on the floor, jammed together.
[winter] Spilled hot soup in my lap. Warm for a moment, wet for an hour.
[afterraid] No table and no chairs since the fight. We ate wherever we sat down.

warm.li: We ate shoulder to shoulder on the floor tonight, elbows in each other's bowls, and I laughed more than I have all week.

blunt.li: A table. Planks. Legs. Do it.

cheerful.li: Floor supper again. I've named my favorite floorboard.

gloomy.li: Another meal off my knees. I've stopped minding, and that's worse.

cold.li: We have the wood for a table. What we lack is anyone who'll build it.

plain.li: [spring] Flowers on the dining table tonight. Someone picked them on the way in.
[spring] Supper in the dining room with the windows open. You could smell the fields.
[spring] Long table, fresh greens, and the first warm evening of the year.
[summer] The dining room stays cool when the rest of the colony bakes. Lingered over supper.
[summer] Ate late in the dining room, with the door open to the evening.
[summer] Supper at the long table, and someone had put out a bowl of berries.
[fall] Harvest supper in the dining room. Every seat full, and every plate too.
[fall] Rain on the windows and a warm meal at a good table.
[fall] The dining room smells of woodsmoke and bread this time of year.
[winter] Frost on the windows, and the long table warm and full.
[winter] Stayed in the dining room long after supper, putting off the walk out into the cold.
[winter] The dining room was the brightest place in the colony tonight.
[highmood] Stayed at the table till the candles were stubs. Didn't want the evening to end.

warm.li: Passed the bread down the long table and it came back empty. I didn't mind one bit.

blunt.li: Good table. Good chairs. More of this.

cheerful.li: Supper in the dining room again. I could get used to being civilized.

gloomy.li: A fine room to eat in. I ate fast anyway, out of habit.

cold.li: A proper dining room keeps people talking at the table. I learn a great deal there.

plain.li: [spring] Rain all week, and nothing to do inside but wait for it to stop.
[spring] Everyone's busy with the planting but me. I've swept the same floor three times.
[spring] Watched the clouds all afternoon. One looked like a muffalo.
[summer] Too hot to work and nothing to do instead. Lay in the shade counting flies.
[summer] Sat outside after supper with nothing to do until the insects drove me in.
[summer] Skipped stones on the water by myself until the light went.
[fall] Rainy evening. I've cleaned every tool I own.
[fall] The harvest's in and suddenly there's nothing to do. I miss it.
[fall] Sat and watched the leaves come down. It took all evening.
[winter] Nothing to do but sit indoors. I've counted the jars in the kitchen. Forty-one.
[winter] Long winter night. I tied knots in a rope and untied them again.
[winter] Too cold to go out, nothing to do in. I talked to the fire.
[lowtech] No one has played a tune in days. I tried humming one and lost interest halfway.

warm.li: Bored, so I helped the cook peel roots. We talked the whole time, and it stopped being boring.

blunt.li: Nothing to do. Again.

cheerful.li: Nothing to do, so I invented a game with pebbles. The rules change every time I lose.

gloomy.li: The days are all the same shape. I keep waiting for one that isn't.

cold.li: Idle hours breed trouble. I've seen it before.

plain.li: [spring] Spring rain all day. Planted in it, hauled in it, ate in it.
[spring] The fields are mud to the ankle, and I'm mud to the knee.
[spring] Every path is a stream this time of year. I gave up on dry feet by noon.
[summer] A summer storm caught us in the field. Warm rain, at least.
[summer] Got soaked, dried off in the sun, got soaked again.
[summer] Fell in the river cooling off. On purpose, the first time.
[fall] Cold rain. My coat has been wet for three days.
[fall] Hauled the harvest in through the rain. The baskets doubled in weight.
[fall] Wet leaves, wet boots, wet everything.
[winter] Sleet all afternoon. It finds the gap at your collar every time.
[winter] Melting snow dripped through the roof onto my bed.
[winter] Wet clothes freeze stiff out here. My sleeves crackle when I bend my arms.
[rain] The rain stopped long enough for me to wring out my socks. Then it started again.

warm.li: Came in soaked, and someone had kept the fire going for whoever came in last.

blunt.li: Wet again. Put a roof over the path.

cheerful.li: Fell in a puddle so big I could have swum in it.

gloomy.li: Wet and cold to the bone. I'll be sick by morning, I'd bet on it.

cold.li: Our boots and coats don't keep the water out. That's a supply problem, not a weather problem.

plain.li: [spring] Rain on the roof, then someone up to check it, then the rain again.
[spring] The birds start at dawn now, and so does someone's hammering.
[spring] Someone came in muddy at midnight, then swore at the mud.
[summer] Too hot with the door shut, too loud with it open. I got neither sleep nor air.
[summer] Insects buzzing all night, and someone up hunting them with a shoe.
[summer] Woke at dawn to people heading out early to beat the heat.
[fall] The wind banged the shutters half the night, and someone kept getting up to fix them.
[fall] Somebody came back late from the fields and tripped over every bed on the way in.
[fall] The roof leaks now, and someone moved a bucket under it, loudly, in the middle of the night.
[winter] People kept getting up to feed the fire. Every time: the door, the cold, the door.
[winter] Someone's cough kept the whole room up.
[winter] Snow slid off the roof in the night with a thump like a falling cow.
[storm] Thunder rattled the walls, and someone counted the seconds out loud.

warm.li: Got up in the night to calm whoever was crying. I didn't sleep much, but they did.

blunt.li: Woken again. Moving my bed to the storeroom.

cheerful.li: Woke up four times. At least I remember all my dreams now.

gloomy.li: I don't really sleep anymore. I just lie there between interruptions.

cold.li: Night traffic past my bed: six times. I've spoken to the one responsible.

plain.li: [spring] {OTHER_nameDef} said my rows were the straightest in the field. I looked, and they were.
[spring] Out planting, {OTHER_nameDef} said it was good to have me alongside. I worked harder all afternoon.
[spring] {OTHER_nameDef} brought me the first wild berries of the year, because I'd worked hardest that week.
[summer] {OTHER_nameDef} said I looked well today. It's the sun, mostly, but I'll take it.
[summer] In the heat of the afternoon, {OTHER_nameDef} told me I'd done the work of two. I needed that.
[summer] {OTHER_nameDef} saved me a cup of cool water and said I'd earned it.
[fall] {OTHER_nameDef} said the harvest wouldn't have come in without me. It would have, but I liked hearing it.
[fall] {OTHER_nameDef} thanked me for the stores I'd laid by. I didn't think anyone had noticed.
[fall] {OTHER_nameDef} said I'd carried the colony through the hard part of the year. I'm keeping that one.
[winter] On a cold night, {OTHER_nameDef} said I make the place feel warmer. I went to bed smiling.
[winter] {OTHER_nameDef} told me my stew was the best thing about winter.
[winter] {OTHER_nameDef} stopped by the fire to say I'd been a great help all week.
[grieving] {OTHER_nameDef} said something gentle about the one we lost, and about me. I needed both.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} said something kind, I said something kind back, and we both stood there smiling.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} thanked me. Good. I earned it.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} called me the best part of the colony. I'm going to be unbearable tomorrow.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} said I matter here. I'd like to believe it.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} praised my work where others could hear. Useful.

plain.li: [spring] Rainy evening, so the games room filled up with wet coats and steaming boots.
[spring] Played cards by the open window. You could hear the frogs.
[spring] An evening in the rec room after a day of planting. My back was grateful.
[summer] The rec room was cooler than outside, so it was packed.
[summer] Long light evening. We played until we couldn't see the board.
[summer] Played games until midnight, since it was too warm to sleep anyway.
[fall] The harvest's in. We celebrated in the games room until late.
[fall] Wet evening, and the rec room so full I sat on the windowsill.
[fall] Played dice with the old hands and lost a week's worth of bragging rights.
[winter] Cold outside, dice inside. I won twice and lost my socks.
[winter] Long winter evening in the games room. We played until the fire was down to coals.
[winter] Someone taught me a new card game. I still don't know the rules, and I won.
[highmood] Laughed so hard at the games table that I had to go outside to stop.

warm.li: Let the young one win at cards tonight. They knew, I think. They didn't mind.

blunt.li: Games room. Won. Bed.

cheerful.li: Finally beat the colony's best chess player. I'm keeping the board just as it was.

gloomy.li: The games room was loud tonight. I sat in the corner and let it be loud around me.

cold.li: Watched who cheats at cards. Two of them. I'll remember.

plain.li: [spring] Last year's stores are nearly gone and this year's crop isn't in. The hungry season.
[spring] Ate wild greens off the riverbank. Bitter, but it's food.
[spring] Planting all day on a thin breakfast. My stomach complained the whole time.
[summer] The garden's growing, but nothing's ripe yet. I keep checking.
[summer] Too hot to eat at noon, then hungry all night.
[summer] Picked a few berries on the way back. Ate them before I reached the door.
[fall] Hauling the harvest all day, and none of it ready to eat. Torture.
[fall] Missed supper bringing in the last field. The cook kept nothing back.
[fall] Smelled bread baking all afternoon and didn't get any.
[winter] The stew is thin and getting thinner.
[winter] I dream about food now. Last night it was a whole roast.
[winter] We're all hungry, and not one of us says so at the table.
[lowmood] Hungry and miserable, and I can't tell which is causing which.

warm.li: Split my supper with someone hungrier. Neither of us full, both of us fed.

blunt.li: More food. Less talk.

cheerful.li: My stomach growled so loudly at supper that the whole table laughed, me too.

gloomy.li: Hungry again. I've stopped mentioning it.

cold.li: Less food in, the same work out. Those sums don't hold for long.

plain.li: [spring] Spring by the calendar, winter in the bedroom. Frost on the floor again.
[spring] Warm days, cold nights. The nights haven't heard it's spring.
[spring] Woke shivering. The fire was out and the window was open.
[summer] Even now the room goes cold after midnight, and I'd put the blanket away.
[summer] Slept with the window open for the heat and woke up frozen.
[summer] A cold snap in summer, and our winter things packed away at the bottom of the chest.
[fall] First frost on the inside of the window. Winter's coming.
[fall] Brought out the winter blankets. They're already not enough.
[fall] The wind has turned northerly, and my blanket is no match for it.
[winter] Woke with frost in my hair where my breath froze on the pillow.
[winter] Slept with my boots in the bed so they wouldn't freeze.
[winter] Cold so deep the walls creaked all night.
[snow] Snow sifted through the roof onto the blanket. I shook it off twice.

warm.li: Shared a blanket with the one next to me. We both slept better.

blunt.li: Cold room. Cold bed. Cold me.

cheerful.li: So cold I slept in my hat and mittens. Very dignified.

gloomy.li: Cold all night. My bones still remember it.

cold.li: The room loses its heat through the north wall. I can show anyone exactly where.

plain.li: [spring] A hot spell already, and the room holds it all night.
[spring] Too warm to sleep, and too early in the year to have seen it coming.
[spring] Spring heat and nowhere for it to go. The windows don't open.
[summer] Slept with the door open for air, and something walked in during the night.
[summer] The walls give back the day's heat all night long.
[summer] I'm sleeping in the yard from now on.
[fall] Late heat this year. The room was an oven again.
[fall] A warm night after we'd packed the summer things away. Sweated through the winter blanket.
[fall] Too hot to sleep, even this late in the year.
[winter] Someone built the fire up too high and the room was stifling. Then it went out and we froze.
[winter] Too hot by the hearth, too cold by the door. I slept in the middle and got both.
[winter] Winter outside and the room baking inside. Someone needs to learn about fires.
[hot] Too hot for work today and too hot for sleep tonight.

warm.li: Fanned the youngest to sleep with a plate. Got an hour myself after.

blunt.li: Hot room. Again.

cheerful.li: Slept on the roof to catch a breeze. Best night in a week.

gloomy.li: Lay in my own sweat all night. I'm too tired to be angry about it.

cold.li: The room has no draft through it. A window at each end would fix it, and I've said so twice.

plain.li: [spring] Watered the first rows this morning. I can't wait to see what comes up.
[spring] Our first spring here. I keep walking out to look at the seedlings.
[summer] Built a bench outside the door today. We sat on it in the evening as if we'd always lived here.
[summer] Swam in the river after work. This place has good water.
[fall] Stacked the first firewood for winter. It looked like more than it was, but it's a start.
[fall] The first harvest is small, but it's ours.
[winter] Frost on our own roof. That's new.
[winter] We kept the fire going all night between us. I think we can do this.
[highmood] Good day, good people. I'm hopeful, and I'm not used to that.

warm.li: Taught the others a song from home tonight. It felt like making the place ours.

blunt.li: Good land. Good people. Work to do.

cheerful.li: I love it here already. Even the mud.

gloomy.li: Things are going well. I'm trying not to count on it.

cold.li: Early hope is cheap. The first winter will tell us who we have.

plain.li: [spring] Flatbread and wild greens for breakfast, still warm from the pan. A good start to a long day.
[spring] Fresh meat and the first herbs of spring tonight. The cook was proud of it, and rightly.
[spring] First supper outdoors this year. It tasted better for it.
[summer] Fresh berries after supper. I could have eaten twice as many.
[summer] Bread and cold fruit on the step, once the heat had gone out of the day.
[summer] Roast corn straight from the fire, with butter running down my chin.
[fall] Harvest stew, thick enough to stand a spoon in.
[fall] Baked squash and fresh bread tonight. The kitchen smelled of it all afternoon.
[fall] We ate the first of the new potatoes, and someone made a little speech about them.
[winter] Hot stew after a day in the cold. I held the bowl just for the warmth.
[winter] The cook opened a jar of the summer preserves tonight. It tasted of long evenings.
[winter] Meat pie on a cold night. Nothing better.
[clear] Ate on the step under a clear sky, with a full bowl and nowhere to be.
[highmood] Had seconds, then thirds, then sat back with my hands on my belly like an old king.

warm.li: Saved the best piece for the one who cooked it. They tried to give it back.

blunt.li: Ate well. Wanted more. Got more.

cheerful.li: Best meal in weeks! I asked the cook what was in it and got told to mind my own business.

gloomy.li: A good meal. I made it last, the way you do when you don't know when the next one is coming.

cold.li: The cook has improved. I've said so, which should keep it up.

plain.li: [spring] {OTHER_nameDef} told me about {OTHER_possessive} mother while we mended the fence. I'd never asked.
[spring] On the woodpile with {OTHER_nameDef} after supper, talking about the people we used to be.
[spring] Sat out in the spring evening with {OTHER_nameDef} until the frogs drowned us out.
[summer] {OTHER_nameDef} and I sat in the shade at noon and told each other things we'd never told anyone.
[summer] Swam in the river with {OTHER_nameDef} and talked on the bank until dark.
[summer] Watched the sun go down with {OTHER_nameDef}, talking about where we'd go if we could go anywhere.
[fall] Husking corn with {OTHER_nameDef}, and somewhere in the middle of the pile we started talking about home.
[fall] {OTHER_nameDef} told me about someone {OTHER_pronoun} lost long ago. We sat with that for a while.
[fall] Rainy evening by the fire with {OTHER_nameDef}. We talked until it needed feeding, and then kept on.
[winter] Shut in by the cold with {OTHER_nameDef}. We talked about everything, then about nothing, then slept.
[winter] {OTHER_nameDef} and I shared a blanket by the fire and talked about what we're afraid of.
[winter] Long night with {OTHER_nameDef}, talking about the winters we nearly didn't get through.
[clear] Lay on the grass with {OTHER_nameDef} under a clear sky, naming the stars wrong on purpose.

warm.li: I told {OTHER_nameDef} I was glad {OTHER_pronoun} came here, and {OTHER_nameDef} said the same, and meant it.

blunt.li: Talked with {OTHER_nameDef}. Real talk. Rare.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I stayed up talking so late we watched the sun come up.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} asked me what I'm afraid of, and I told the truth. I feel lighter. I also feel like I've left a door open.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} trusts me now. I'll be worthy of it, or careful with it.

plain.li: [good,spring] Wildflowers along every path this week. Somebody's been planting them on purpose.
[good,summer] The garden is at its best, and so is the colony, for once.
[good,winter] Frost on the roofs and a clean, swept hall. The colony looked like a picture tonight.
[bad,spring] The thaw has turned the yard to mud, and the mud has got everywhere.
[bad,summer] Flies over the refuse heap. You can smell it from the kitchen door.
[bad,fall] Dead leaves in every corner of the hall, and the broom nowhere to be found.

warm.li: [good] Someone has been sweeping the paths every morning. I'd like to know who, to thank them.
[good] The new carving by the door makes people smile on their way in. I've watched.
[good] Sat on the bench outside after supper and just looked at the place for a while.
[good] Someone's put a cup of water and two flowers on every sill. I counted them on my way to bed.
[good] The colony looks cared for. A bit of that is my doing, and I'm proud of my bit.
[good] The hall is clean and bright tonight. I said so to the cook, who did most of it.
[bad] Carried the rubble out of the hall myself, one basket at a time, before supper.
[bad] The yard's a mess. I'll ask if a few of us can spend a morning on it together.
[bad] It's grim around here lately. I put the one nice thing I own where everyone can see it.
[bad] The place is worn down, like the rest of us. I patched the doorframe tonight, which is a start.
[bad] Scrubbed a stain off the hall floor tonight. One down.
[bad] The walls are bare and the floor is dirt. I keep thinking of ways to make it nicer.

blunt.li: [good] Clean hall. Who did it? Do it again.
[good] Pretty place lately. Don't spoil it.
[good] Good-looking colony. Took long enough.
[good] Flowers, rugs, a statue. Fine. I like it.
[good] The place looks right for once.
[good] Someone swept. Noticed.
[bad] Mud in the hall. Wipe your boots.
[bad] The yard stinks. Clear it.
[bad] Ugly as sin around here.
[bad] Rubbish by the door for three days. Three.
[bad] Bare walls, dirty floors. Do better.
[bad] This place looks like we're about to leave it.

cheerful.li: [good] The hall looks so nice now that I keep finding excuses to walk through it.
[good] Somebody hung a painting by the stairs. I said good morning to it.
[good] Flowers in the window, sun on the floor. I sat down in the middle of it for a minute.
[good] The colony's never looked better. I want to show it off to someone.
[good] The new rug is so soft I took my boots off just to walk across it.
[good] Clean paths and blooming beds. I think the place is happy, if places can be happy.
[bad] The hall's a mess, so I've started a game: everyone carries one thing out on their way past.
[bad] Ugly old wall, so I drew a sun on it in charcoal. Much better.
[bad] Mud everywhere. I've decided it's a very large garden that hasn't started yet.
[bad] It's dreary around here, so I picked flowers for the table. Weeds, mostly, but pretty ones.
[bad] Dirty floors today. Tomorrow I'm going to scrub one room and see who copies me.
[bad] Grim week for the look of the place. Next week will be better, I've decided.

gloomy.li: [good] The colony looks fine. Fine things get noticed by the wrong people.
[good] Someone's made the hall lovely. I sat in it and felt a bit less heavy.
[good] The flowers by the door are out. I looked at them and thought of someone who isn't here.
[good] Clean and pretty for once. I almost forgot what's out past the walls.
[good] It's a nice place now. I'm not sure I've earned living in it.
[good] The garden's blooming. I walked through it twice and still felt tired.
[bad] Grime and rubble in every corner. I stepped over the same pile four times today.
[bad] Ugly walls, ugly weather. It all runs together.
[bad] There's a stain on the hall floor that's been there since the fight. We all step round it.
[bad] Another board came loose in the hall today. The last one's still loose too.
[bad] Mud and refuse. It's hard to feel like a person in a place like this.
[bad] Everything here is gray, and getting grayer.

cold.li: [good] The colony's looks are improving. Our trading position will follow.
[good] Clean halls, decent art. People behave better in pleasant rooms. I've seen it.
[good] The place looks prosperous. Visitors will price us accordingly.
[good] A good-looking colony keeps its people. That's the practical case for flowers.
[good] The hall looks well kept. I know who keeps it, and I've made a note of it.
[good] Pleasant surroundings today. I worked faster in them.
[bad] The yard is a disgrace. Anyone visiting would think we're failing.
[bad] Filth slows people down and makes them sick. I've seen both this week.
[bad] Ugly rooms make for short tempers. I've counted three arguments this week.
[bad] Rubble left where it fell. Somebody decided it wasn't their job.
[bad] The colony looks neglected, and neglect invites trouble.
[bad] Dirt in the hall for days. I know who walks through it most.

plain.li: [good,spring] Opened the window in my room at last. Slept with the smell of rain.
[good,fall] My room is warm and dry while the wind tries the shutters. I fell asleep listening to it fail.
[bad,spring] Water came under the wall of my room in the night. My boots were floating.
[bad,fall] Leaves blew in under my door again. My room's half outside.

warm.li: [good] My room is starting to feel like mine. I put the little carving from a friend on the shelf.
[good] Woke up rested in my own room, with the light coming in just right.
[good] Someone fixed the draft in my room while I was out. I'll find out who.
[good] Lay in bed a few minutes longer than I should have, just because I could.
[good] My room's quiet and warm. I said a small thank-you before I slept.
[good] Put a blanket from home on the bed. Now the room smells right.
[bad] My room's cold and plain, but it's a start. I'll make something of it.
[bad] The wall by my bed weeps when it rains. I've hung a cloth over it.
[bad] The roof drips over my bed, so I moved the bed. Small room, small problem.
[bad] It isn't much of a room. Someone offered to help me fix the walls, which helped already.
[bad] My room's dark and damp. I left the door open to share the hall's warmth.
[bad] Ugly room. I hung up a drawing the youngest made me, and now there's one thing in it worth looking at.

blunt.li: [good] Good bed. Slept straight through.
[good] My room. My door. Good.
[good] Room's warm. Nothing to add.
[good] Slept well. Room's right.
[good] Finally a room worth the name.
[good] Quiet room. Best thing here.
[bad] Room's cold. Fix the wall.
[bad] Damp bed again.
[bad] My room's a box. A bad one.
[bad] Leaky roof. Right over the pillow.
[bad] Can't sleep in that room. Moving out.
[bad] Bare walls, cold floor, no sleep.

cheerful.li: [good] Woke up in my lovely room and lay there grinning at the ceiling.
[good] My room's so cozy I've started going to bed early on purpose.
[good] I rearranged my room again. It's even better now, which I didn't think was possible.
[good] Slept so well I woke up singing.
[good] My room is my favorite place in the world, and I've been to a few places.
[good] There's a bird that sits on my windowsill every morning. I think it likes my room too.
[bad] My room's drafty, so I sleep in my coat. It's like camping, but with a roof.
[bad] Tiny room. I can touch both walls from the bed, which is a good trick for parties.
[bad] The roof leaks right over my bed, so now I have a water clock.
[bad] My room is ugly, so I've given every crack in the wall a name.
[bad] Cold room, warm blankets. I'm calling that a draw!
[bad] My room smells of damp, so I filled it with pine branches. Now it smells of damp pine.

gloomy.li: [good] Slept the whole night through. Woke up not knowing where I was.
[good] A good room. It's the one thing here I'd be sorry to lose.
[good] Quiet night in my room. For a few hours I wasn't afraid of anything.
[good] My room is warm. I lay there thinking of the ones out on watch.
[good] Woke rested for once, and lay there a long while before getting up to face it all.
[good] The room is nice. I keep it tidy as if someone might come and take it.
[bad] Cold room, damp blanket, long night.
[bad] My room smells of mildew. So do I, now.
[bad] Lay awake in that bare room thinking about every room I've lost.
[bad] The walls of my room are too close. I dream about them.
[bad] Woke up cold again. I've stopped expecting otherwise.
[bad] This room is where I go to be tired.

cold.li: [good] My room is in order. A person who sleeps well makes fewer mistakes.
[good] The door locks and the walls hold heat. That's all I ask of a room.
[good] Good rest in a good room. The council got this one right.
[good] I've arranged my room exactly to my liking. Anyone who moves anything will hear from me.
[good] My room is better than most. I'm aware of it, and so is everyone else.
[good] Slept seven hours without a sound. A well-built room.
[bad] My room is substandard. I've measured it against the others.
[bad] Cold and damp. Whoever built this room should sleep in it.
[bad] A room like this costs the colony my best work.
[bad] Poor room again. I'm keeping count of the nights.
[bad] The walls let in the wind. I've shown three people the gaps.
[bad] I was given this room. I'll remember who gave it to me.
